headword: {一抹|いちまつ}の{不安|ふあん}
gloss: a touch of anxiety; a slight unease

definitions.gloss: a touch of anxiety; a slight unease; a lingering worry
definitions.explanation: A faint but persistent feeling of worry or concern. The word {一抹|いちまつ} means "a trace" or "a touch," so the expression conveys a small but nagging sense of unease.

examples.japanese: {一抹|いちまつ}の{不安|ふあん}を{感|かん}じる。
examples.english: I feel a touch of anxiety.

examples.japanese: {計画|けいかく}は{順調|じゅんちょう}だが、{一抹|いちまつ}の{不安|ふあん}が{残|のこ}る。
examples.english: The plan is going well, but a slight unease remains.

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しい{仕事|しごと}への{期待|きたい}と{同時|どうじ}に、うまくやれるかどうか{一抹|いちまつ}の{不安|ふあん}もあった。
examples.english: Along with excitement about the new job, there was also a slight worry about whether I could do well.

notes:
USAGE:
{一抹|いちまつ} literally means "one stroke" (of a brush), evoking the image of a thin, faint line. The expression is semi-literary and often appears in written Japanese, news articles, and formal speech. It conveys worry that is small but cannot be dismissed.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {一抹|いちまつ}の{不安|ふあん}を{感|かん}じる (to feel a touch of anxiety)
- {一抹|いちまつ}の{不安|ふあん}が{残|のこ}る (a slight unease remains)
- {一抹|いちまつ}の{不安|ふあん}を{覚|おぼ}える (to sense a slight unease)
- {一抹|いちまつ}の{寂|さび}しさ (a touch of loneliness — {一抹|いちまつ} can modify other feelings too)
